newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Brent CFDs ease off highs, nothing in chains.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Brent CFDs ease off highs, nothing in chains.

text.p: Brent CFDs eased off highs made in the wake of two early Brent deals at strong premiums, but traders said that the North Sea market looked well supported.
Two Brent cargoes loading March 14-16 traded this morning at April Brent +55 cents. One of the cargoes was deferred from March 13-15 while the other was advanced from March 15-17.
The sole Brent cargo scheduled to load March 14-16 in the orginal loading programme was advanced to March 13-15 and kept by the equity holder on Wednesday.
Prompt CFDs failed to match the levels seen in the wet market, but next week's dates (March 3-7) jumped up after the physical deals were done to trade at April Brent +29 cents.
CFD values eased in the afternoon with March 3-7 trading at April Brent +21 cents and March 10-14 at April +6/9.
Outright April Brent paper slipped to talk around $19.50 a barrel in line with the IPE screen, having traded earlier at $19.70. The April/May spread traded at +33 cents.
The buyer of the two Brents now holds some eight cargoes and was heard to be working two VLCCs to South Africa.
Traders said that the buyer was keen to bid the market up to support a long swaps position.
But most agreed that North Sea market was in general fairly strong after brisk trade in the last couple of days cleared out a lot of March barrels.
"The market looks in good shape. You can't bid a weak market up, but you can accentuate it if you want to go in a certain direction," said one trader.
In the Mediterranean, traders said an end-Feb loading Iraqi Kirkuk cargo was sold into Portugal.
